rejected.title: Imperialism
card: Imperialism is when one country takes control of other lands and peoples. The stronger country rules the weaker one, or shapes its government and economy.
Imperial powers often wanted raw materials, new markets for their goods, and land for settlers. Some also wanted power and status among rival nations.
By 1914 European powers ruled much of Africa, Asia and the Pacific. Britain ruled more territory than any other power.
The people who lived in these lands often had little or no say in how they were ruled.
rejected.remember: Imperial powers ruled others, often for their own gain. By 1914 Britain ruled the most.

a.q: Which situation is an example of imperialism?
opts: A European power seizes African land and rules its people
Two countries agree to trade freely and keep their own laws
A country welcomes migrants who choose to settle there
A country gives aid to another and then withdraws
a.why: Imperialism is one country taking control of other lands and peoples. In the trade agreement, both countries keep control of themselves, so no one is ruling the other.
a.clue: Look for one country ruling another's land and people.

b.q: Why did many European powers want colonies in Africa and Asia before 1914?
opts: To gain raw materials, markets and status over rivals
To help the local people win independence quickly
To keep their own populations from moving abroad
To share power equally with local rulers
b.why: Imperial powers wanted raw materials, markets for their goods and standing among rival nations. Helping local people gain independence is wrong because imperial rule gave them little or no say.
b.clue: Think about what the ruling country gained.

a.q: Norland and Varia are two made-up countries. Which event would be an example of imperialism?
opts: Norland takes over Varia and appoints its governors
Norland and Varia sign a deal to trade more freely
Norland lends Varia money, and Varia pays it all back
Norland and Varia join forces against a rival
a.why: Imperialism means one country taking control of another's land and people, and appointing Varia's governors puts Norland in charge. A trade deal is tempting because imperial powers wanted markets, but in a deal both countries still run themselves.
a.clue: After each event, who is in charge of Varia?

b.q: A European government in the late 1800s argues that it needs more colonies. What did imperial powers often hope to gain from them?
opts: Raw materials, markets and status among rivals
Independence for the local people they had ruled
Equal power shared with the local rulers they met
Lasting peace treaties with every rival nation
b.why: Imperial powers often wanted raw materials, markets for their goods, land for settlers and standing among rival nations. Independence for local people is wrong because people under imperial rule often had little or no say.
b.clue: Think about what the ruling country got out of it.

a.best: Norland takes over Varia and appoints its governors

b.best: Raw materials, markets and status among rivals
